elements.text: Failure of the flight crew to execute a missed approach when visual cues for the runway were not distinct and identifiable
Crew’s decision to descend to the instrument landing system decision height instead of the localizer (glideslope out) minimum descent altitude
First officer’s long landing on a short contaminated runway
Crew’s failure to use reverse thrust and braking to their maximum effectiveness
Captain’s fatigue, which affected his ability to effectively plan for and monitor the approach and landing
Shuttle America’s failure to administer an attendance policy that permitted flight crewmembers to call in as fatigued without fear of reprisals
Recommendation to require simulator training for decision-making for rejected landings below 50 feet
Recommendation to require simulator training for maximum performance landings on contaminated runways
Recommendation to require written policy emphasizing immediate missed approach upon go-around callout
Recommendation to develop standardized policy allowing crew to decline assignments if impaired by lack of sleep
Recommendation to require operators to adopt and provide details of the fatigue policy
